target.title: fix(macos): prevent hatch and web chat from timing out on slow first replies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where macOS onboarding/web chat could make a slow first assistant reply look stuck or prematurely timed out when the selected model takes longer than the old client-side budget. This matters for first-run hatch/chat paths with slower models such as OpenAI 5.5, where the user expects the assistant to keep working after they describe its purpose.

The mismatch was that the macOS WebChat path needed a longer assistant-run budget and a completion observation path, while the request/ACK deadline should still fail quickly when the gateway is unreachable.

## Why This Change Was Made

This separates the short request/ACK deadline from the actual WebChat assistant run budget. The shared `GatewayConnection.chatSend` default stays request-sized so other macOS callers such as Talk Mode keep their existing timeout policy, while `MacGatewayChatTransport.sendMessage` explicitly opts WebChat/hatch into a five-minute `timeoutMs` run budget.

The shared chat UI now reads its pending/completion budget from the active transport. The default transport budget remains 120 seconds, while macOS WebChat overrides it to five minutes and waits for completion through the existing Gateway `agent.wait` surface before refreshing history. The change does not alter gateway protocol shape, auth, provider routing, model selection, session storage, schema, migrations, or delivery channels.

## User Impact

macOS users hatching or chatting with a newly configured assistant now get a realistic wait window and a production completion observation path for slow first replies instead of a premature timeout or stuck-looking state while the assistant run may still be active or recently completed.

The intended behavior is that macOS WebChat/hatch keeps gateway ACK failures prompt while giving only the WebChat assistant run, UI pending state, and completion refresh path the first-run-sized five-minute window.

## Evidence

Latest conflict-resolution validation after rebasing onto current `origin/main`:

```text
PASS: no conflict markers in PR files
PASS: ChatViewModel keeps main arm-id protection and transport-scoped timeout
PASS: shared transport default remains 120000ms
PASS: macOS WebChat opts into five-minute completion wait
PASS: tests cover default and mac-sized timeout budgets
```

```text
diff_check=clean
merge_tree=clean
changed_files=6
```

Timeout-scope regression proof from the final scope fix:

```text
PASS: GatewayConnection.chatSend default is request-sized
PASS: MacGatewayChatTransport explicitly opts into 300000ms
PASS: low-level default regression expects 30000
PASS: mac transport regression expects 300000
PASS: shared transport default remains 120000ms
PASS: tests cover default and mac-sized timeout budgets
```

The timeout-scope check was first run as a RED proof before the production fix and failed with:

```text
RED: timeout scope invariant not satisfied
- GatewayConnection.chatSend default is not request-sized
- MacGatewayChatTransport.sendMessage does not explicitly opt into 300000ms
```

Regression coverage added or updated:

- `apps/macos/Tests/OpenClawIPCTests/GatewayConnectionControlTests.swift` asserts the low-level `GatewayConnection.chatSend` default remains request-sized, `MacGatewayChatTransport.sendMessage` sends `timeoutMs == 300_000`, macOS WebChat delegates completion waits to Gateway `agent.wait`, and `agent.wait` receives the supplied run ID and timeout.
- `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Tests/OpenClawKitTests/ChatViewModelTests.swift` asserts the shared chat default completion wait remains `120_000` ms, an injected transport can raise that wait to `300_000` ms, non-terminal send ACKs remain pending by default, and the terminal `ok` ACK case stays explicit.

Local Swift execution is unavailable in this Linux environment:

```text
swift unavailable: command not found
swiftformat unavailable: command not found
xcodebuild unavailable: command not found
```

Hosted macOS CI should execute the Swift tests and formatter on the updated PR head.
